html:
Part III transitions from the algebraic and geometric mechanisms of Parts I–II to the concrete physical spectra realized across the archimedean wall \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. To keep the theoretical derivation distinct from the empirical scorecard, Part III separates the two tasks explicitly: this chapter derives the structural laws governing elementary fermions, composite hadrons, emergence of the Hartree and Bohr atomic scales, periodic-table shell closures, the Diophantine stability valley, and decay-lifetime recurrences, whereas the following chapter, Physical Observations, confronts the resulting numerical predictions at q_0 \approx 1.1100 with CODATA 2022, PDG 2024, and AME 2020 measurements and specifies falsifiable experimental protocols.

Within the five-step categorical pipeline (Category -> Hecke/Markov Algebra -> Hyperbolic/Bring Geometry -> Archimedean Period Realization -> Physical Spectra), this chapter proceeds across six structural stages:

  1. Elementary fermions, pair production, and composite nucleons: Embeddable knot generators on the exceptional divisor classify the first-generation leptons (e^\pm, \nu_e, \bar\nu_e), while Breit–Wheeler pair creation (\gamma\gamma \to e^+e^-) and Frobenius Gram selection on H_3(q) assemble quarks into mesons and Borromean-linked nucleons (p, n).
  2. Torus-knot force carriers, electromagnetic completeness, and Hartree/Bohr scale emergence: The genus-4 geometry of Bring's surface selects T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} as the unique torus-knot force carriers; two-strand spectral completeness determines the fine-structure constant \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}(q), from which the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} derives the categorical Hartree energy E_{\mathrm{Hartree}} and Bohr radius a_0.
  3. Bloch-group dilogarithms and colour falsifiability: The Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2, the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z), and the five-term Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon on the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) anchor the analytic mass tower and the multiplicative running of \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}.
  4. The Diophantine stability valley and hadron half-life laws: Integer minimization of the mass functional defines the Diophantine valley of stability in the (Z, N) plane, while single-crossing skein transitions, q-self-corrections, and skein–Coulomb enhancements yield closed half-life formulas across \beta-emitters.
  5. Composite atomic shells and the periodic table: Eigenvalues of the electron-strand transfer operator and the Rumer–Jones canonical inner product organize electronic orbitals, characterizing noble-gas shell closures and metallic character across the periodic table.
  6. Volume-tower transcendence, Picard–Lefschetz / Seiberg–Witten duality, and spectrahedral rigidity: Borel–Zagier volume transcendence, the golden-quartet Galois orbit, D_4 moduli symmetry, and the convex geometry of the Hecke spectrahedron complete the analytic structure of the predicted spectrum.

This opening section defines the first-generation lepton knot assignments—the electron and positron words \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 and \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (closures: the positive and negative Hopf links; the trefoils 3_1, \overline{3_1} are kept as a backup) and the neutrino unknot modes—tabulates their pairwise linking and crossing relations, and closes with the Borromean-quark conjecture: a quark is a neutrino unknot trapped in a colour tube of Bring's surface, and three of them link Borromean-style into a baryon.
